name: Localized Lichen Myxedematosus with Monoclonal Gammopathy or Systemic Symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Localized Lichen Myxedematosus with Monoclonal Gammopathy

criteria.description: Presence of localized waxy, firm papules or plaques with sclerodermoid changes
Detection of monoclonal gammopathy (usually IgG lambda) in serum electrophoresis
Skin biopsy showing mucin deposition with fibroblast proliferation and fibrosis
Presence of systemic manifestations such as arthralgia, myopathy, or dysphagia
No clinical or laboratory evidence of thyroid dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (cutaneous lesions, monoclonal gammopathy, and characteristic histopathology) must be met; systemic symptoms support diagnosis but are not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of systemic scleromyxedema and thyroid-related mucinoses is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically firm, waxy papules or plaques localized to the limbs or trunk

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous mucin deposition with sclerodermoid changes

searchTerms: mild joint pain in small joints
skin feels thick and firm in one spot

common.symptomName: Mild myopathy with proximal muscle weakness

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema localized to affected areas
Mild fatigue related to systemic involvement

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to systemic involvement
searchTerms: renal impairment due to body-wide involvement

laboratory: Serum protein electrophoresis showing monoclonal gammopathy (IgG lambda)
Mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in systemic cases
imaging: MRI may show soft tissue thickening in affected areas
Chest X-ray or echocardiogram if systemic involvement suspected
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating mucin deposition, fibroblast proliferation, and fibrosis
Negative autoimmune serologies (ANA, anti-Scl-70) to exclude scleroderma

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized skin involvement rather than localized
More frequent systemic involvement including severe myopathy and neurologic symptoms
Higher risk of fatal systemic complications
Associated with thyroid dysfunction (usually hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism)
Localized pretibial myxedema without monoclonal gammopathy
Different histopathological findings with less fibroblast proliferation

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin induration beyond localized areas
Development of severe systemic symptoms such as dysphagia or cardiac conduction abnormalities
Emergence of neuropathy or renal impairment
references: Wollina U, et al. Localized lichen myxedematosus with monoclonal gammopathy: clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2019.
Patterson JW. Dermatopathology of mucinoses. Dermatol Clin. 2017.
Orphanet: Localized lichen myxedematosus with monoclonal gammopathy or systemic symptoms. ORPHA:90399.
